articles.title: More Cases, Less Autonomy? The Paradox of Modern Orthopaedic Residency Training.
articles.authors: Scuderi GR, Reichmister JP, Smitterberg CW, Mont MA
articles.population: Orthopaedic residents and training programmes
articles.outcomes: Operative autonomy, clinical ownership, competency measures, readiness for independent practice
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic residents are performing more operations than previous generations, but this has not translated into greater clinical independence or ability to manage complications. The authors argue that surgical training needs to measure competency and autonomy directly, not just case numbers, to ensure graduates can independently manage patients.

articles.title: Trends in Adult Reconstruction Fellowship Applications and Match Outcomes: A Report From the American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons Fellowship Committee.
articles.authors: Ledford CK, Parks NL, Hamilton AC, Taunton MJ, Hamilton WG
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of fellowship application trends
articles.population: Adult reconstruction hip and knee surgery fellowship applicants and programs
articles.sample_size: 236 fellowship positions across 114 programmes in 2026; mean 267 applicants per year
articles.outcomes: Fellowship match rates, unfilled positions, successful matching by applicant type (US MD versus foreign medical graduates), and top-choice programme matching rates
articles.take_home: Adult reconstruction fellowship positions have grown by 17% over the study period, but unfilled positions have increased sharply to 16% in 2025, suggesting more positions are being created than there is applicant interest. Whilst US-trained doctors have very high match success rates (96%), the overall matching landscape is changing, with more applicants securing their preferred programme in recent years.

articles.title: RESULT-Hip. The impact of restrictive compared with liberal transfusion strategy on cardiac injury and death in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture : protocol for a multicentre, randomized controlled trial of two blood transfusion strategies.
articles.authors: Sinclair RCF, Beveridge G, Duckworth AD, Giddings A, Cholbi S, Guy GV, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and over with hip fracture and anaemia undergoing surgery
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: death or major adverse cardiac events (including myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery). Secondary outcomes: all-cause mortality, quality of life at 120 days, cost-effectiveness and health economic evaluation
articles.take_home: This is a trial protocol describing a planned study comparing two blood transfusion strategies in older hip fracture patients. The study aims to determine whether giving more blood transfusions to correct anaemia reduces heart-related complications and death compared with giving fewer transfusions.

articles.title: Plasma calprotectin as infection biomarker in hip fracture patients: a prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Pyrhonen HS, Tham J, Stefansdottir A, Persson A, Malmgren L, Rogmark C
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and over who had surgery for hip fracture
articles.outcomes: Detection of infection within 7 and 30 days after hip fracture surgery using blood biomarkers (calprotectin, procalcitonin, C-reactive protein, white blood cell count)
articles.take_home: Calprotectin was better at detecting infections after hip fracture surgery than other blood tests, particularly for infections occurring within 7 days, but it still only had moderate accuracy overall. White blood cell count performed similarly to calprotectin, whilst the other tests were less useful.

articles.title: The use of patellar tendon autograft and lateral meniscus repair are associated with loss of motion of the knee among female patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Dadoo S, Nash AE, Yang Z, Aycardi N, Bhardwaj N, Vyas D, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 14 years and over undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Subsequent surgery for loss of knee motion within mean follow-up of 2.3 years
articles.take_home: Female patients who had ACL surgery using patellar tendon graft and lateral meniscus repair were more likely to need further surgery for stiffness, with combined use of both significantly increasing this risk. These factors did not increase risk in male patients.

articles.title: Long-term survivorship of medial meniscus posterior horn repair during revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: 10-year results from the SANTI Group.
articles.authors: Santamaria F, Wehbe H, Ayata M, Pioger C, Sonnery-Cottet V, Campos JP, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with medial meniscus posterior horn repair
articles.outcomes: Secondary medial meniscectomy rate at 10 years; comparison of suture-hook repair versus other repair techniques
articles.take_home: About 1 in 6 patients needed further surgery to remove the repaired meniscus within 10 years. Although suture-hook repair appeared slightly better initially, the difference was not statistically significant after accounting for other factors.

articles.title: Cross-cultural adaptation and initial evaluation of selected measurement properties of the simplified chinese version of the knee injury and osteoarthritis outcome score joint replacement in patients with knee osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Wang W, Sun Y, Zhou P, Zhou L, Massengo Ngoyi DMA, Sulistiawan F, et al.
articles.study_type: Cross-cultural adaptation and measurement validation study
articles.population: Patients with knee osteoarthritis scheduled for total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Data completeness, floor and ceiling effects, internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha 0.849), test-retest reliability (intraclass correlation 0.791), measurement error (smallest detectable change 11.69 points), and construct validity (correlation with IKDC r = 0.766)
articles.take_home: The simplified Chinese version of the KOOS-JR questionnaire is reliable and valid for measuring knee outcomes in Chinese patients before knee replacement surgery. The questionnaire showed good consistency when repeated after 10-14 days and strongly correlated with another established knee assessment tool.

articles.title: Reduced knee adduction moments in bicruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty compared with bicruciate-substituting designs: A contralateral within-patient study.
articles.authors: Hakukawa S, Niki Y, Harato K, Nishizawa K, Kaneda K, Matsumoto T, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing simultaneous bilateral total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Knee adduction moments during walking, alignment measurements, and patient-reported outcomes including Forgotten Joint Score-12
articles.take_home: Bicruciate-retaining knee replacements produced lower loading forces across the knee joint during walking compared with bicruciate-substituting designs, although patients reported similar satisfaction and outcomes with both types.

articles.title: Preoperative Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Use is Associated With Increased Complication Risk After Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Dose-Response Analysis.
articles.authors: Alfonsi SP, Zickler CL, Yadav AS, Ahmad F, Terhune EB, Burnett RA
articles.study_type: Retrospective claims database analysis with matched cohort comparison
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement, aged approximately 65 years on average
articles.sample_size: 77,958 SSRI users matched to 233,277 controls (total 311,235 patients)
articles.outcomes: 2-year complication rates including component loosening, periprosthetic fracture, periprosthetic joint infection, dislocation, and revision surgery; revision-free survival
articles.take_home: Patients taking SSRIs before hip replacement had higher complication rates within 2 years, including infections, dislocations, fractures and loosening of the implant. However, the risk did not increase with higher SSRI doses, suggesting SSRIs may not directly cause these problems.

articles.title: Multiple-Offset Titanium Slot-Stems Versus Limited-Offset Cobalt-Chromium Stems in Hybrid-Fixation Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Comparative Study With 5- to 14-Year Follow-up.
articles.authors: Boontanapibul K, Chankong K, Susrivaraput C, Pongcharoen B, Pinsornsak P, Tammachote N
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty with hybrid fixation
articles.sample_size: 63 revision knee replacements (39 multiple-offset titanium and 24 limited-offset cobalt-chromium)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes (modified WOMAC and Knee Society Score), knee flexion, stem-tip pain, implant survivorship, radiographic measurements including component overhang and joint-line level
articles.take_home: Multiple-offset titanium stems reduced stem-tip pain and improved how the implant fitted to the bone compared to limited-offset cobalt-chromium stems, but these technical improvements did not lead to better pain relief or knee function for patients, and both implant types had similar long-term survival rates.

articles.title: Comparison of CT-based migration analysis against radiostereometric analysis for assessing two-year migration in an uncemented medial pivot tibial knee implant : clinical implications from a prospective safety study.
articles.authors: Engseth LHW, Conrad CJ, Ohrn FD, Schulz A, Rohrl SMH
articles.population: Patients receiving an uncemented medial pivot knee implant
articles.outcomes: Maximum total point motion at 24 months using three migration analysis methods; range of motion; Forgotten Joint Score; Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Score; radiation dose; procedure time
articles.take_home: The uncemented knee implant showed stable migration over two years with all three measurement methods, indicating it is safe to use. CT-based imaging detected lower migration values than traditional radiographic methods, though all methods produced stable results over time.

articles.title: Operative Outcomes of Cemented Hip Arthroplasty: An Examination of the French Paradox.
articles.authors: Pisquiy JJ, Booth M, Agard T, DelBello R, Mattam B, Dietz MJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing hip arthroplasty with a wedge-taper femoral stem system
articles.outcomes: Implant failure rates, subsidence, aseptic loosening, intraoperative fractures, bone cement implantation syndrome, readmission rates
articles.take_home: Cemented hip replacements using the French Paradox technique had lower subsidence (3.71mm versus 5.16mm) compared to uncemented stems, with similar readmission rates and fracture rates between groups. This suggests cemented hip replacements with this technique are effective and reliable.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence across the continuum of care for the aging musculoskeletal patient: From longitudinal phenotyping to personalized surgery and recovery monitoring.
articles.authors: Oettl FC, Zsidai B, Pruneski JA, Oeding JF, Longo UG, Hirschmann MT, et al.
articles.population: Older adults with musculoskeletal conditions
articles.outcomes: AI applications across the full care pathway including disease prediction, surgical planning, perioperative risk assessment and postoperative recovery monitoring
articles.take_home: Current artificial intelligence in orthopaedic surgery focuses on isolated tasks, but the field needs to develop systems that support older patients across the entire journey of care, from predicting who will get worse to personalising surgery and tracking recovery at home. For AI to be trusted in clinical practice, it must be transparent, validated properly, and integrated into workflows with proper monitoring after deployment.

articles.title: Low graft failure after primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction in professional soccer players: A retrospective cohort study of 232 knees from the SANTI Study Group.
articles.authors: Santamaria F, Santos PM, Ayata M, Wehbe H, Sonnery-Cottet V, Campos JP, et al.
articles.population: Professional soccer players undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Graft failure (symptomatic rupture), reoperations, contralateral ACL injury, time to graft failure
articles.take_home: Professional soccer players had good long-term results after ACL reconstruction, with only 5.6% experiencing graft failure over an average of 8 years. Adding a lateral extra-articular procedure appeared to reduce graft failure, though the difference was not statistically proven.

articles.title: Sex-related differences after ACL reconstruction differ between early functional recovery and 5-year outcomes.
articles.authors: Marty-Diloy T, Graveleau N, Bouguennec N
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary ACL reconstruction between January 2017 and December 2019
articles.outcomes: 6-month quadriceps strength and hop-test performance; 5-year return to sport, Tegner activity score, IKDC score, ACL-RSI psychological score, and recovery of preinjury activity level
articles.take_home: Men showed better early muscle strength after ACL surgery, and at 5 years were more likely to return to their preinjury activity levels and had better subjective knee scores than women, although both sexes had similar overall return-to-sport rates. This suggests that men and women recover differently after ACL reconstruction, with differences appearing more in psychological readiness and activity levels rather than simply whether patients return to sport.

articles.title: Visual presentation, statistical reporting and methodological considerations in a meta-analysis of remnant-preserving anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Xiong Q, Wang X, Fu W
articles.population: Studies on remnant-preserving anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Clinical stability outcomes
articles.take_home: This letter identifies statistical reporting errors and visual presentation problems in a previous meta-analysis of knee ligament surgery, and provides a corrected analysis to help clinicians better understand the actual evidence.

articles.title: Proximal fibular osteotomy for medial compartment knee osteoarthritis: clinical effectiveness and biomechanical rationale: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Edmonds CJ, Duru D, Olamona VB, Soni D, McDonnell SM, Radhamony N
articles.population: Patients with medial compartment knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 2,855 knees across 45 studies (38 clinical studies and 7 biomechanical/anatomical studies)
articles.outcomes: Pain, function, patient-reported outcome measures, radiographic joint space width, operative time, hospital stay, blood loss, complications including common peroneal nerve dysfunction, and biomechanical loading patterns
articles.take_home: Proximal fibular osteotomy appears to reduce pain and improve function in people with medial compartment knee osteoarthritis, with quick recovery times, although the improvement works by shifting load away from the damaged area rather than fixing the underlying damage. The evidence is limited by inconsistent study designs and a lack of long-term comparison data, and there is a risk of nerve damage that needs careful monitoring.

articles.title: A 15-year evaluation of two total knee arthroplasty designs : similar patient-reported outcomes and survivorship but divergent patellofemoral and radiological outcomes.
articles.authors: Clement ND, Williamson TR, Leitch GL, Scott CEH, Gaston P
articles.population: Patients who had primary total knee replacement surgery
articles.sample_size: 61 patients completed functional assessment at 15 years
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (Oxford Knee Score, Forgotten Joint Score, EQ-5D), pain scores, implant survivorship, radiological findings
articles.take_home: Two different knee replacement implants performed similarly overall at 15 years, with both giving patients better function and pain relief than before surgery, though scores did decline slightly over time. One implant had more anterior knee pain and some radiological changes, but this did not translate into clinically important differences in how well patients were doing.

articles.title: Autogenous Cancellous Bone Impaction Grafting Is a Viable Technique for Managing Acetabular Bone Defects Observed During Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty in Crowe Types III and IV Hip Dysplasia Cases.
articles.authors: Kawasaki M, Okura T, Futatsugi R, Maeda K, Tachi H, Fujibayashi T, et al.
articles.population: Patients with severe developmental dysplasia of the hip (Crowe types III and IV) undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 35 hip replacements (18 receiving cancellous bone impaction grafts, 17 receiving structural bone grafts)
articles.outcomes: Operative time, graft integration speed, bone resorption, osteolysis volume, implant stability, and clinical outcomes over 12 to 17 years
articles.take_home: Cancellous bone impaction grafting is a viable technique for managing severe hip dysplasia during hip replacement, with faster bone integration and less bone loss compared to structural bone grafting, whilst maintaining similar long-term outcomes over at least 12 years.

articles.title: Expert Perspectives on Disruptive Bleeding and Hemostasis Optimization in Primary and Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Structured Expert-Opinion Survey.
articles.authors: Mont MA, Chen AF, Smitterberg CW, Aflatooni JO, Cohen-Rosenblum AR, Della Valle CJ, et al.
articles.population: Arthroplasty surgeons experienced in primary and revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Definition and characterisation of disruptive bleeding, risk factors, intraoperative and postoperative management triggers, and use of topical haemostatic agents
articles.take_home: Surgeons agreed that disruptive bleeding after hip replacement should be defined by care-altering events such as significant drops in blood count, need for transfusion, prolonged drainage or return to theatre, rather than by specific blood loss amounts. Key risk factors included low platelet counts and anticoagulant use.

articles.title: Preoperative coronal phenotype is associated with the initial balance state but only weakly with final balance in robot-assisted TKA.
articles.authors: Morita Y, Mylonakis N, Shin J, El-Hassan M, Shichman I, Kenanidis E, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 429 knees for initial analyses; 389 for final and change analyses
articles.outcomes: Initial and final intraoperative medial and lateral gap balance in extension and flexion; relationship between preoperative knee alignment and structural changes with balance state
articles.take_home: Preoperative knee alignment and structural changes only weakly predict how well the knee is balanced during robot-assisted knee replacement surgery. The findings suggest that surgeons need to assess balance directly during the operation rather than relying on preoperative measurements alone.

articles.title: Greater three-dimensional cam burden and superolateral location are associated with end-stage hip osteoarthritis: A retrospective comparative study.
articles.authors: Igrek S, Yigit O, Canbaz SB, Yilmaz H, Ozgur EG, Eceviz E, et al.
articles.population: Cam-positive hips: patients undergoing hip replacement for primary osteoarthritis, and elderly patients aged 65 years or older treated for femoral fractures without osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 438 cam-positive hips (126 with osteoarthritis, 312 without osteoarthritis)
articles.outcomes: Three-dimensional cam morphology measurements including alpha angle, cam volume, cam-to-head volume ratio, and lesion location
articles.take_home: Hips with end-stage osteoarthritis had larger cam lesions and were more likely to have lesions positioned in the superolateral part of the hip socket compared to non-arthritic hips. However, this study shows an association only and does not prove that larger cams cause osteoarthritis in individual patients.

articles.title: Previous bariatric surgery before knee arthroplasty: A cautious interpretation.
articles.authors: Qu X, Sun G, Chen B
articles.study_type: Commentary on a register-based observational study
articles.population: Patients who underwent knee arthroplasty, some with previous bariatric surgery
articles.outcomes: Reintervention rates after knee arthroplasty at 2 years
articles.take_home: The original study found no clear difference in reintervention rates between patients who had bariatric surgery before knee replacement and those who did not, but this commentary suggests the findings should be interpreted cautiously because of study limitations such as short follow-up time and selection bias.

articles.title: Substantial improvement in short-term survivorship in patients receiving robotic arm-assisted medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty : a retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Cheok T, Law K, Vermeir JF, Jaarsma RL, Doornberg JN, Silva AM
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty with isolated medial compartmental osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision rate, hospital length of stay, surgical duration, superficial surgical site infection, periprosthetic joint infection
articles.take_home: Robotic arm-assisted knee replacement had a 78% lower revision rate compared with conventional surgery and shorter hospital stays. There was no difference in infection rates or operating time between the two approaches.
